I read all 380 commits and the 127-PR sheet. 114 of the commits are dependency bumps and ~230 more are refactor/test/ci/chore churn. Only **36 commits** (1 feat, 26 fix, 9 perf) touch behavior, and they collapse into far fewer user-facing lines because the same fix landed across several modules.

## What actually changed for users

**The one feature:** webhook deliveries now retry with exponential backoff (`395fb48`, #4191). It touched `src/webhooks/dispatch.js` *and* `src/core/config.js`, so it almost certainly added a config knob you should name in the notes.

**Three things that are breaking but aren't labeled that way** — this is the part I'd push back on before you publish:

1. `fix(auth): return 401 for an expired token instead of 403` (`1d2bd55`, #4223). Anyone branching on 403 breaks. It's tagged `fix`, but it's a contract change.
2. `refactor(api): drop the unused v1 export route` (`56dc828`, #4152). "Unused" is an internal judgment; it removed a route from `router.js` + `handlers.js`. If it was reachable, it's a removal.
3. `fix(store|core): use the right units in the latency histogram` (`59402bc`, `1f2bc4e`). Correct, but every dashboard and alert threshold on that metric now reads differently.

Plus a fourth I can't resolve from the log: **`stop re-exporting the internal error types`** landed 8 times across db, core, billing, auth, and jobs. If any of those types were reachable from the package entrypoint, that's a breaking import change. Worth 60 seconds with `git show` on `src/core/errors.js` before you cut.

## Draft entry

```markdown
## 4.2.0 — 2026-08-29

### Breaking
- An expired token now returns 401 instead of 403. Clients that branch on
  403 to distinguish "expired" from "forbidden" need updating.
- The latency histogram now reports the correct units. Existing dashboards
  and alert thresholds against it will need rescaling.
- The v1 export route has been removed.

### Added
- Failed webhook deliveries are retried with exponential backoff.

### Fixed
- The trace id is now preserved across a retry.
- Paginating past the last page no longer fails on a null cursor.
- An empty allowlist is now treated as empty rather than as no filter.
- Request bodies are no longer written to the logs.
- The HTTP client clears its timer when the socket drops, and closes the
  pool on shutdown.
- A duplicate header is no longer sent on retried requests.
- URLs with a trailing slash are no longer double-trimmed.
- Token parser errors now say what was actually wrong.
```

Two judgment calls in that draft: I merged per-module duplicates (the null-cursor fix landed in api, db, queue and webhooks separately) into one line each, since users see one symptom. And I dropped all 9 `perf` commits — they're micro-optimizations (skip a JSON round-trip, avoid a clone, batch metric writes) with no measured numbers in the log. If someone has benchmarks, one line is worth adding; without numbers it's noise.

## Before you publish

- **Node minimum.** Five separate `docs: note the minimum node version` commits, CI moved to node 22, `.nvmrc` pinned three times. If `engines` changed in `package.json`, that's a Breaking line and it's currently missing. The log doesn't show me the field contents.
- **`pull the request id out of the logger context`** (http, db, store, queue — 4 commits). "Pull out of" reads both ways. If the request id left your log lines, log consumers care.
- **Runtime dep bumps.** fastify, pg, knex, ioredis, pino, zod, nanoid, dotenv and undici all moved — all patch/minor. The other 7 (eslint, vitest, esbuild, typescript, tsx, prettier, husky) are dev-only and don't belong in the notes. Your call whether the runtime set gets a one-liner; your 4.1 entry didn't do this, so I left it out.
- **The PR sheet has duplicates.** #4120/#4121 are the same pino bump by different authors, same for #4124/#4125 and #4126/#4131. Doesn't affect the notes, but the sheet will overcount if you're quoting a PR number anywhere.
